S11.01.note: The plan gives no code location; the only label I checked was the Copy message fallback, and I did not survey all controls.
steps: Turn on VoiceOver (Cmd+F5) and move through the chat with VO+Arrow keys.
Stop on the Copy message button under a reply and listen for its spoken name, compared with Expected.

S11.02.note: Heading markup is inner structure; I only checked the Agent activity section label.
steps: Turn on VoiceOver and open the VO rotor (VO+U), then choose Headings.
Open a chat with tool activity and check for a top heading and nested section headings, compared with Expected.

S11.03.note: The Account menu trigger label was not confirmed; the Keyboard shortcuts item is in its menu.
steps: Click outside any field, press Tab repeatedly and watch focus move to each control.
Open the Account menu and use the Down and Up arrow keys to move between items.
Press Escape and check the menu closes and focus returns to its button.
S11.03.where: Any screen after sign-in > press Tab to move through controls, use arrow keys in open menus, press Escape to close them; press Cmd+K (Ctrl+K on Windows) to open the command palette

S11.04.note: Focus styling is a CSS rule, not a control.
steps: On a chat screen, press Tab one time at a time.
Check that the focused control shows a clear ring or outline each time, compared with Expected.

S11.05.note: I confirmed the menu item text but not that it opens a dialog; the Account menu trigger label was not confirmed.
steps: Open the Account menu and choose Keyboard shortcuts.
Press Tab several times and check focus stays inside the dialog.
Press Escape and check the dialog closes.
S11.05.where: Account menu > Keyboard shortcuts (opens from the Account menu on any screen)

S11.06.note: Same caveat as S11.05 about the dialog and trigger label.
steps: Click the Account menu button and note which control has focus.
Open Keyboard shortcuts, then close it with Escape.
Check focus returned to the Account menu button, compared with Expected.
S11.06.where: Account menu > Keyboard shortcuts, then close it

S11.07.needs: a screen reader (VoiceOver) and a signed-in account
S11.07.note: The announcement is a polite live region; I did not confirm which events are announced.
steps: Turn on VoiceOver and send a message that uses a tool.
Keep focus in the composer and listen for a short spoken status when the reply or tool step finishes, compared with Expected.

S11.08.needs: a screen reader (VoiceOver) and a signed-in account
S11.08.note: Behaviour is in the streaming announcer component; not verified live.
steps: Turn on VoiceOver and send a question that gets a long streamed reply.
Listen while the reply streams and check it is spoken in short chunks or once at the end, not word by word, compared with Expected.

labels.text: This tool requires approval before execution.

S11.09.needs: a signed-in account where a tool asks for approval
S11.09.note: The Allow and Deny labels come from a shared constant I did not open; how to trigger an approval depends on the account's tool approval setting.
steps: Send a request that asks the AI to use a tool that needs approval.
Look at the tool card and read the warning line about approval.
Turn on VoiceOver and check the running, done or waiting state is spoken, and that the Allow and Deny buttons have names, compared with Expected.
S11.09.where: Chat > send a request that needs a tool approval > watch the tool card in the reply

S11.10.needs: a touch screen or phone-width browser to check the touch case
S11.10.note: The code shows the row is always visible on touch devices; the tap-to-show path was not checked.
steps: Send a message and wait for a reply.
Move the pointer over the reply and look for the action row with Copy message.
On a touch screen (or phone width), tap the reply and check the action row is always visible, compared with Expected.
S11.10.where: Chat > send a message > hover over the reply > Copy message button in the row under it

S11.11.note: Not found in time: I did not open apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerFilesMenu.tsx or the drag handling in ArtifactsPanel.tsx to get the visible menu words.

S11.12.note: The app control offers Small, Default and Large only; the 200% OS text setting is not part of this control.
steps: Open Settings and choose Appearance.
Set Chat text size to Large.
Look at the chat text and check it grows without being cut off, compared with Expected.

S11.13.note: Zoom keys for the Electron window were not verified in the code.
steps: Zoom the app window in (the browser zoom keys, if the app supports them).
Check that at high zoom the chat shows one column and does not scroll sideways, compared with Expected.

S11.14.needs: none (optionally turn on Reduce motion in the operating system)
S11.14.note: The OS setting also applies through System, per the code comment.
steps: Open Settings and choose Appearance.
Under Motion, choose Reduced.
Send a chat message and watch the reply animations and any looping indicators, compared with Expected.

S11.15.needs: a microphone and a signed-in account
S11.15.note: The button that opens the In this chat menu during a call was not confirmed.
steps: Click the Start voice mode button in the chat composer and allow the microphone.
Open the in-call menu titled In this chat and turn on Captions.
Speak a sentence and check that caption lines appear in the captions panel, compared with Expected.
S11.15.where: Start voice mode (composer button) > voice call screen > the menu with In this chat > Captions

S11.16.needs: a microphone and a signed-in account
S11.16.note: Code shows each voice turn is written into the chat as a message.
steps: Start voice mode and allow the microphone.
Say two or three sentences and then end the call.
Open the same chat and check the spoken turns appear as readable text, compared with Expected.
S11.16.where: Start voice mode > speak > end the call > the conversation in the chat

S11.17.note: The chart's name and table labels are built from the chart title, so no fixed visible words were found.
steps: Ask the AI for a bar chart of a short list of numbers.
Find the chart card in the reply and check it has a title.
Turn on VoiceOver and check the chart name and the data table are read, compared with Expected.
S11.17.where: Chat > ask for a chart (for example a bar chart of sample numbers) > the chart card in the reply

S11.19.note: Navigation group name General and the Arabic menu entry were not directly confirmed in the picker code.
steps: Open Settings and choose General.
Under Display Language, choose Arabic (or another right-to-left language).
Look at the whole screen and check menus, text and spacing mirror to the right, compared with Expected.

S11.20.note: Direction is set per paragraph in code; not verified visually.
steps: Type an English sentence, press Shift+Enter, then type an Arabic sentence.
Send the message.
Check each paragraph in the reply bubble runs in its own direction, compared with Expected.
S11.20.where: Chat composer > type a line in English, a line in Arabic, then send

S11.21.needs: a Japanese, Chinese or Korean input method
S11.21.note: Inner keyboard behaviour; the composer checks for composition before sending.
steps: Add a Japanese (or Chinese or Korean) input method on the Mac and switch to it.
In the chat composer, type a word and press Enter to confirm a conversion candidate.
Check the message is not sent and the text stays in the composer, compared with Expected.

S11.22.needs: none (a passkey or linked device helps)
S11.22.note: Dates use the browser locale; the exact visible navigation label was not found.
steps: Open Settings and go to the section with Passkeys or linked devices.
Look at the dates shown next to a device or passkey.
Change Display Language in General, return and compare the date format with Expected.
S11.22.where: Settings > the section that lists Passkeys and linked devices (exact navigation label not confirmed)

S11.23.note: Money is formatted with the browser locale; visible price labels were not extracted.
steps: Open the pricing page of the web app.
Read the plan prices and note the currency symbol and number format.
Compare with Expected (right currency symbol and the user's number format).
S11.23.where: Pricing page (web app /pricing) for plan prices

S11.24.note: The Sidebar > Scheduled path was taken from the request example, not confirmed in the code.
steps: Create a scheduled task with a repeat interval of 1 and then 2 hours.
Read the schedule card label.
Check singular and plural forms read correctly, compared with Expected.
S11.24.where: Schedules (Sidebar > Scheduled) > New task > set the repeat to Every 2 hours (or Every 1 minute) and save

labels.text: You appear to be offline. Check your connection.

S11.25.needs: a way to go offline and, for other languages, Settings > General > Display Language
S11.25.note: The message is translated through the errors namespace; other languages were not checked.
steps: Turn off the Mac's Wi-Fi.
Send a chat message.
Read the error and compare it with Expected (in the chosen language).
S11.25.where: Turn off Wi-Fi, then send a message in Chat; read the error shown in the chat

S11.26.note: The Account menu trigger label was not confirmed; the hint is built by shortcutLabel in packages/ui/ui/src/platformKeys.ts.
steps: Open the Account menu and look at the Keyboard shortcuts item.
Read the hint on its right and compare it with Expected (command symbol on Mac, Ctrl elsewhere).
S11.26.where: Account menu > Keyboard shortcuts (the shortcut hint on the right of the item)
